current_status.stage: Approved & marketed — US (Brixadi, commercialized by Braeburn under exclusive license from Camurus) and EU/global (same molecule marketed by Camurus directly as Buvidal); unconfirmed press reports since Sept 2025 that Camurus is in talks to acquire Braeburn and reclaim full US rights
current_status.partner: Braeburn (exclusive US license since 2014 agreement); Camurus is platform owner/EU-global marketer
current_status.data_point: Q2 2026: Brixadi royalties to Camurus SEK 127M (+42% YoY, +20% QoQ); Brixadi held ~32% share of US LAI buprenorphine equivalized units in Q1 2026, vs 26% a year earlier

finding_history.summary: Press reports said Camurus was in talks to acquire its US commercialization partner Braeburn, aiming to regain full US rights to Brixadi (Camurus estimated untapped US market potential at >$1B). Neither company confirmed the talks or disclosed financial terms.

Camurus Q1 2026 interim report: Brixadi royalties SEK 106M, up 44% YoY; Brixadi reached ~32% share of US LAI buprenorphine equivalized units vs 26% a year earlier. Management attributed a softer sequential quarter to annual payor authorization renewals, expecting growth to normalize through the rest of 2026.

Braeburn announced two oral presentations and two posters on Brixadi at the 88th Annual CPDD Meeting (June 13-17, 2026, Portland OR), covering first-dose withdrawal suppression, real-world treatment retention vs. sublingual buprenorphine in patients with recent fentanyl use, and real-world dispensing/utilization trends.

Camurus Q2 2026 interim report: Brixadi royalties SEK 127M, up 42% YoY and 20% sequentially, contributing to record overall product sales; growth attributed to rising US demand and Braeburn's expanded commercial organization, alongside continued Buvidal growth in Europe.
